title: SLO-driven trace sampler diary
content:
Purpose:
This is a working diary for running an SLO-aligned trace sampling experiment across production routes. Goal: capture representative p50/p95/p99 stage breakdowns without saturating storage or blowing through retention budgets. Use results to prioritize low-hanging scheduling and batching fixes for the 1-3s tail.

Background/context:
- We have recurring customer reports of occasional 2–6s tail responses on hosted routes that normally sit at 200–400ms p50.
- Prior analyses (bench vs prod) show attention kernels and emit handoffs both contribute, but attribution varies by seq_len and cold/warm cache state.
- Current full-trace capture is expensive; we need an SLO-driven sampler to increase signal at p95/p99 while keeping costs modest.

Sampling strategy (high level):
- Tiered sampling windows keyed by route SLA and recent error/latency spikes.
- Base sample rate: 0.1% across all traffic for long-term baselines.
- Elevated windows: when route p95 > SLO*1.1 or error rate > 0.5%, increase to 2% for 10m.
- Tail focus: run 100% capture for individual requests that exceed 1s (ad-hoc) but limit to N/day per route.
- Sequence-aware boost: for seq_len >= 512 boost sampling by x10 to catch long-token behavior.
- Coldstart tagging: mark traces where instance_uptime < 120s or kv-cache_miss_ratio > 0.6.

Implementation notes and flags (teams):
- sampler.v2.enabled = true (feature flag for progressive rollout)
- sampler.v2.route-policy = slo-driven
- trace.max_size_bytes = 1MB (hard cap)

Data schema captured per trace (minimum):
- request_id, route, model_variant, seq_len, coldstart, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, queue_wait_ms, tokenize_ms, kv_lookup_ms, attention_ms, emit_ms, egress_ms, total_ms, timestamp
- tags: snippet of prompt hash, customer_tier (free/paid/enterprise)

Quick synthetic cohort table (sampled day 2025-02-25):
(plain text CSV style)
cohort,requests,sampled,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,median_batch,avg_kv_miss
short-<128,120k,120,210,480,820,1,0.05
mid-128-512,21k,210,310,920,1400,2,0.12
long->=512,3k,90,610,1800,4200,3,0.48
coldstart-any,9k,180,420,1600,3600,1,0.62

Selected observations (from diary runs):
1) Short requests (p95 ~480ms): emit_ms ~200–300ms contributes ~40–60% of tail. Emit stalls correlate with downstream egress retries to ISTIO (5xx) — need circuit-breaking telemetry join.
2) Mid-length (p95 ~920ms): batch wait + attention kernel dominate. For p95 traces where batch_size=1, attention_ms is still high (gpu scheduling jitter).
3) Long sequences (p95 1800ms, p99 4200ms): kv_lookup misses and cache-populated synchronous fetches cause amplification. When kv_cache_miss_ratio > 0.4, median kv_lookup_ms jumps from 12ms -> 320ms.
4) Coldstart traces: when instance_uptime <120s, p99 often dominated by model load and cold kv miss cascade; observed spikes 2–6x baseline.

Per-stage breakdown (example aggregate for long->=512 cohort p99):
- ingress (TLS + routing): 35ms
- tokenize: 48ms
- queue_wait / batcher wait: 430ms
- kv_lookup (sync): 780ms
- attention compute: 1250ms
- emit handoff & serialization: 420ms
- egress + network: 150ms
- total observed: ~3163ms (numbers from sample day)

Hypotheses and immediate experiments (ranked):
A) kv-sync-to-async: converting the largest synchronous kv paths to optimistic async with best-effort fallback will reduce tail in long sequences. Experiment: enable optimistic async on a canary route (10% of long requests) and compare p95/p99 after 48h. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/981
B) batcher threshold tuning: lower max wait threshold for routes with high seq_len variance. Experiment: dynamic wait threshold based on recent seq_len distribution (start at 20ms -> reduce to 5ms for targeted route). Measure p95 change and throughput impact.
C) emit backpressure instrumentation: add counters for emit->egress handoff retries and expose per-route alert. Short cohort shows large variance here. Quick fix: more aggressive egress connection pool sizing for high-SLA routes.
D) coldstart mitigation: pre-warm pools for enterprise routes during business hours; introduce a tiny warm-up cache for KV keys seen in last 5m.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are attention kernel jitter issues correlated with multi-tenancy on node GPUs (noisy neighbors)? Need node-level GPU telemetry join.
- How stable is kv cache miss behavior across regions? Current samples are NA-heavy.
- Does our sampler bias toward problematic requests (bootstrap problem)? need to validate sampling representativeness for p50 baseline.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Arjun: wire optimistic-async KV path into canary and add metric kv.optimistic.enabled (JIRA-ENG-4123) — target: 2025-02-26
- Sofia: run batcher threshold A/B and collect throughput vs p99 tradeoff for three routes — target: 2025-03-03
- Devin: instrument emit->egress retry counters and dashboard for top 10 routes by tail impact — target: 2025-02-24
- Maya (owner): collect regional sampled traces (EU + APAC) and validate cohort distributions; produce follow-up diary entry comparing region differences — target: 2025-03-02

Notes to self (raw):
- Watch for sampler amplification: high seq_len boost + tail-trigger 100% capture can generate many big traces; enforce daily cap per route and per-customer.
- Consider offline replay harness to reconstruct stage timings when partial traces are captured (we have token timestamps in logs).
- Keep an eye on retention cost: evaluate compression of stage times instead of full span payload for long traces.

End of entry.
